evidence_basis: RF1_A_TOFU_NO_R1C: FAIL all four Golden realism gates
RF1_B_TOFU_WITH_R1C: FAIL all four Golden realism gates
RF2_STAGE1_RICE_NO_R1C: PASS all four Golden realism gates
Historical rice granary sample was also materially more credible but is not itself causal proof

topic_conditioned_subvariables.hypothesis: The tokens/semantics that frame a scene as traditional/heritage craft activate stylized heritage-workshop imagery independent of tofu-specific process objects.
current_support: RF1 tofu failures repeatedly contain old-wood/heritage-workshop visual conventions.
Historical tofu prompts and outputs often emphasize traditional workshop identity.
current_counterevidence: RF2 rice candidate was also visually traditional/old-workshop-like yet passed all four gates.
Therefore heritage/traditional semantics alone are unlikely to be sufficient.

minimal_single_variable_test.caveat: Changing workspace era may also alter expected objects/materials; reviewer must reject if semantic substitution necessarily changes multiple physical scene constraints.

topic_conditioned_subvariables.hypothesis: The tofu-making object/process schema itself (cloth-lined mold, pressing frame, curd/tofu, vats/troughs) triggers canonical explanatory staging and photogenic craft treatment.
current_support: RF1 A fails without R1C while retaining tofu-specific process objects.
Repeated historical tofu outputs show molds, cloth, vats, steaming equipment and finished tofu arranged as legible production evidence.
RF2 rice passes under the same renderer/task structure after replacing the production domain.
current_counterevidence: RF2 changed the entire production domain, so the effect cannot yet be attributed specifically to tofu objects versus moisture/heat or workspace semantics.

minimal_single_variable_test.candidate: traditional/manual seed-cake or dry curd-like pressing is rejected if heritage/moisture differs; preferred intervention must preserve pressing action, workbench, operator distance and spatial density while substituting tofu-specific material/object identity only
minimal_single_variable_test.reviewer_requirement: Approve only if the proposed substitute can be specified without changing wet/steam state, heritage framing, spatial furnishing or task structure.

topic_conditioned_subvariables.hypothesis: Moisture, heat, steam and wet-surface expectations associated with tofu production activate cinematic haze, wet-floor sheen and beautified material treatment.
current_support: RF1 evaluator explicitly identified steam, wet floor and window/side light as a coordinated atmosphere package.
Tofu production plausibly invites wet/steam cues that the renderer can exaggerate.
current_counterevidence: RF1 A prompt did not explicitly require theatrical steam/wet floor; their appearance may arise from tofu-topic schema or general workshop aesthetics.
RF2 rice pass cannot isolate moisture because rice scene is substantially drier.

minimal_single_variable_test.prohibition: Do not add 'no steam', 'dry floor', 'avoid haze' as anti-AI negatives; the event itself must naturally differ in moisture/heat state.
minimal_single_variable_test.caveat: Reviewer must verify that changing the event phase does not also change process-object inventory or scene layout.

topic_conditioned_subvariables.hypothesis: Dense small-workshop production-space semantics encourage the renderer to arrange multiple tools, containers and machines as explanatory set dressing.
current_support: RF1 A/B both fail documentary causality with multiple workshop cues kept legible.
Older tofu evidence also shows complete process-space storytelling.
current_counterevidence: RF2 rice candidate remains a production workspace with machinery, sacks, sieve and broom yet passes.
Therefore production-space furnishing alone is not sufficient.

minimal_single_variable_test.caveat: If reducing furnishing changes 'make the place identifiable' semantics or task structure, the test is confounded and must not run.

causal_ranking_for_design_not_truth.note: This is experimental priority, not a causal verdict.
causal_ranking_for_design_not_truth.rationale: S1 and S4 are weakened because the passing RF2 rice scene still contains traditional/old-workshop and production-space semantics. The remaining discriminating difference is more concentrated in tofu-specific process schema and associated wet/heat state.

frozen_next_minimal_experiment.reason_for_selection: Among feasible single-variable interventions, changing the tofu process phase from wet/hot to dry/cool post-press handling can preserve tofu identity, workspace, renderer, aspect, R1C policy and RF1 task structure more cleanly than replacing the full process-object schema.
frozen_next_minimal_experiment.proposed_candidate: SAME_TOFU_WORKSHOP_AND_PRODUCT_IDENTITY, SAME 9:16 RF1 STRUCTURE, but anchor a dry/cool post-press handling moment rather than the wet/hot pressing context.
prohibited_prompt_changes: Do not add explicit 'no steam', 'dry floor', 'avoid cinematic light', 'less staged', or similar negative/realism instructions.
Do not change renderer, reference policy, aspect, or evaluator.

preregistered_interpretation.RF1_TOFU_WET_FAIL__RF3_TOFU_DRY_FAIL: WET_HEAT_STEAM_STATE_NOT_SUFFICIENT_TO_EXPLAIN_TOPIC EFFECT; tofu process-object schema or other topic-conditioned factors remain unresolved.

stop_conditions: Stop after the one candidate and one Golden absolute-realism evaluation.
No second semantic subvariable under this contract.

required_checks: Does the proposed candidate preserve tofu topic and workshop identity?
Is the only changed semantic subvariable truly the process phase / moisture-heat state?
Can the treatment be expressed without explicit anti-AI/realism negative rules?
Are object inventory, workspace era, task structure, renderer, aspect, reference policy and evaluator held fixed enough for causal interpretation?
Is budget exactly one new image, zero retry?
